parties:

Vs.

full_judgment:
Gobinda Chandra Tagore J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why constituting a 7 (seven) member committee comprising of respondent Nos.2 to 8 under Memo No. 31.036.033.00. 00.221.2010-409(7) dated 27-7-2011 (Annexure-D) issued under the signature of respondent No.9 for investigating the finally published Dhaka City Survey Record-of-Rights in respect of 191 mouzas to ascertain the genuinity of such publication and to uphold/cancel the same and the report of the said committee dated 22-5-2012 (Annexure-E) and also the office order under Memo No. মপ/08/2011/83 dated 26-1-2012 issued by respondent No.10 (Annexure-F) forming two committees to investigate the alleged irregularities of the officials engaged in preparing and finally publishing the said Record-of-Rights, and thereby taking departmental actions against the petitioner and/or to initiate criminal cases under the Anti Corruption Law shall not be declared to have been done/issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents shall not be directed to interfere with the quasi-judicial functions of the field level officers engaged in preparing and finally publishing the Record-of-Rights under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Tenancy Rules, 1955 in any manner, whatsoever other than under the provisions of the aforesaid Act and Rules and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed. 

 3. The respondents were also restrained from giving effect to the recommendations made vide report dated 22-5-2012 (Annexure-E) and the said respondents are also restrained from interfering with the quasi-judicial functions of the field level non cadre officers/employees engaged in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Tenancy Rules, 1955 for a period of 4 (four) months. Subsequently, the order of stay and that of the order of restraint were extended from time to time. 

 4. Shortly stated the relevant facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are as follows: 

 The petitioner No.1 is the President of Assistant Settlement Officer Welfare Association and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are Secretary and Vice-President of the same Association of Dhaka unit. All of them are serving under the office of the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys as Non-Cadre Servants of the Government and were engaged in the preparation and publication of the recent Dhaka City Survey Khatians following the Dhaka City Survey, which were finally prepared and published in the Gazette Notification on different dates. The Directorate of Land Records and Surveys is empowered to prepare and publish the record-of-rights as per order issued by the Government from time to time by issuing Gazette Notification under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The employees and officers engaged in preparation and publication of the record-of-rights of that office are divided into two categories- Non-Cadre Service Holders starting from Chainman to Assistant Settlement Officer i.e. Chainman, Badar Amin, Sarder Amin, Halka Officer/Sub-Assistant Settlement Officer and Assistant Settlement Officer/Circle Officer and the other group belongs to the Cadre Service, who are deputed to the Directorate. The preparation and publication of the record-of-rights are quasi-judicial functions under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Tenancy Rules, 1955, Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935, the Survey Act, 1875 and Technical Rules, 1957. The Rules 26-31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 are the main rules for preparing record-of-rights. Like judicial protection Act, 1850, section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the rule 39 of the Tenancy Rule, 1955 and also the circular No. ভূঃমঃ/শাঃ-২(অডিট আপত্তি)-৭/২০০৬-৩৯০/১(৯০)dated 2-6-2008 issued by the Ministry of Land have given a safeguard to the persons involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. The record-of-rights of Dhaka City Survey of 191 mouzas prepared under the Dhaka City Survey have already been completed and published in the Bangladesh Gazette as per rule 34 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 as well as, as per section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, except some of the khatians of each mouzas against which Writ Petitions or Civil proceedings are pending. When the dispute on finally publishing the record-of-rights were being adjudicated by the Land Survey Tribunals, the Ministry of Land suddenly issued the impugned office order bearing No. 31.036.033.00.00.221. 2010-409 dated 27-7-2011 forming an enquiry committee consisting of the respondent Nos.2-8 for giving an opinion either for affirming or cancelling the finally prepared and published City Survey Khatians of 191 Mouzas under the Dhaka City Survey after 5 years of publication of the same in the Gazette Notification. The said enquiry committee submitted the impugned report dated 22-5-2012 as contained in Annexure-E. In the said report, it was, amongst other, opined that approximately 2815.00 acres of the land of the Government were not recorded in the name of the Government while, most of those properties earlier belonged to the Court of Wards and subsequently, in the name of the private persons by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. On receiving the said report dated 22-5-2012, the respondent No. 10, DGDLRS issued the impugned Memo No. মপ/০৮/২০১১/৮৩ dated 26-1-2012 forming two committees-one consisting of respondent Nos.11-15 and the other consisting of respondent Nos.16-19 to enquire into the matter in order to find out the irregularities in not recording the Government land and also to take action against the persons involved in such preparation and publication of the record-of-rights by starting departmental proceeding as well as by filing anti-corruption case against them. The petitioners being aggrieved by the said impugned orders and enquiry report contained in Annexures D, E and F filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained the Rule and the orders of stay and restraint. 

 5. The respondent No.1, the Ministry of Land contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition by denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the respondents, including the respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are not only responsible for management and administration of the Directorate or they are not only the supervising officer but they are also engaged in preparing and publishing record-of-rights. Therefore, the allegation made by the petitioners that the respondents are interfering with the so-called quasi-judicial function is not true. The superior officers starting from the post of Charge Officer of the DGLRS are legally authorized to supervise the official activities of the sub-ordinates of the Directorate. They also exercise their revenue powers for preparing and publishing of the record-of-rights in accordance with law as well as the instructions of the Government passed from time to time. Section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 authorizes the Board of Land Administration to pass any order for correction of any entry in a record-of-rights maintained under Part-V of the Act or in a settlement-roll prepared and finally published under Part-V thereof. If there is any bonafide mistake, the superior officer of the Directorate may interfere with the functions and activities of the petitioners and others as per the provision of section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; rules 27, 28, 31, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 42A 42B, and 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Technical Rules, and Chapter (iv) Rule 16, 19, 32 and Chapter (viii) rule-20 of Instructions of the Settlement Department, 1957. The position of a DGLRS is clearly manifested in rule 12 of Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935. The Government can issue circulars, memorandums and other instructions as per rules of Business and Allocation of Business and make rules under section 152 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Therefore, issuing circulars etc. by the Government or the Directorate for making it responsible and accountable is within the legal authority of the Government and the Directorate. Section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 provides safeguard to the petitioners and others only if the acts are done in good faith. The circular dated 2-6-2008 was issued as a directive for the audit team to follow the same during auditing the field level offices. Rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 authorizes the Revenue Officer with the additional designation, Settlement Officer or Assistant Settlement Officer to exercise power like a Civil Court. The Rules do not give any immunity to the officials from accountability for their activities. The Revenue Officers and others engaged in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights cannot escape the responsibility and liability in securing the public interest in preparing the records-of-the public property. The respondents have every authority to look into whether the petitioners and others had any negligence or committed any deviation from the assigned tasks in preparing the records-of-land properly. Every judicial or quasi-judicial officer has a right to pass an order but it must be guided by the existing laws. The respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are empowered to exercise revenue powers and accordingly, they can look into the activities of their subordinate officers. The authority can hold any enquiry or form any committee to look into the allegations of any mischief or gross irregularities and negligence or intentionally done wrong activities committed by any of subordinate revenue officers at any stage of the survey. There are allegations published in different dailies that some revenue officers have recorded the land belonged to different public agencies in the name of some unscrupulous private persons although the previous record i.e. RS Record was in the name of public agencies and thus, helped misappropriation of the public lands by the land grabbers. The respondents are constitutionally bound to look into the serious allegations in public interest in order to take appropriate measures for recovery of the public property and also to take punitive measures against the persons found responsible for the misdeeds and causing losses to the state and public in general. There being serious allegation of irregularities against the finally published record-of-rights of 191 mouzas of City Survey, the respondents formed committee to scrutinize/investigate into the legal aspects as to whether there was any scope for cancellation of the records to redress the public sufferings and accordingly, the enquiry committee was formed by the Memo dated 27-7-2011. Moreover, no penal decision was taken against the petitioners. Accordingly, they cannot be aggrieved thereby and come before this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution for that purpose. No law or any rule gives any immunity to any officials involved in doing irregularities in the name of quasi-judicial functions or any public-office-functions. The petitioners having done gross irregularities in publishing the record-of-rights cannot claim the safeguards under the law and circular as has been claimed by them. The impugned orders were very much within the purview of law. The impugned report contains the facts based on the case studies. The petitioners could have sought relief through normal official procedure and there was nothing to worry about the said impugned order and reports unless he or she is found to have done anything wrong in malafide intention. Hence, the Writ Petition is not maintainable. 

 6. Having placed the Writ Petition, Mr Md Khalilur Rahman along with Mr Junaed Hossen Khan and Mr Md Rashidul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the record-of-rights prepared finally has already been published in the official Gazette, the Government including the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to cancel the same and the aggrieved persons including any Government agencies can take recourse to law before the Land Survey Tribunal for correcting the errors, if any, in preparing the said record-of-rights and, as such, the impugned orders as contained in Annexures D and E and the report prepared in pursuance thereof as contained in Annexure-E are liable to be declared to have been passed or prepared without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 7. Then, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and others engaged in preparing and publishing, the record-of-rights being protected by section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as well as by rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 issuance of the impugned orders as contained in Annexure D and F and the enquiry report prepared in pursuance thereof as contained in Annexure-E are liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 15. It appears from the Writ Petition that the petitioners filed the Writ Petition with an apprehension only that upon such enquiry, departmental and punitive measures may be taken against them. But it appears from the said office order dated 26-1-2012, Annexure-F that it was intended not to take punitive measures against all the persons, who were involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights but only against the persons who are liable for committing any irregularity and illegality. Thus, it appears from the said impugned orders as contained in Annexures D, E and F that the Ministry of Land or the Directorate of Land Record and Survey has yet not completed the enquiry fixing the liability of the persons responsible for any illegality. However, once the record-of-rights, whether it was prepared wrongly or rightly has already been published in the official Gazette, the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to cancel the same by any administrative order. The same can only be cancelled or altered or corrected by the competent Court of civil jurisdiction.
